{"choices": [{"finish_reason": "tool_calls", "index": 0, "message": {"content": "The string formatter's `format` is const. Good. So calling `.format(...)` on a const formatter works for all built-in types.

Now, there's a subtle issue. The `do_format` calls `std::get<sizeof...(T) - N>(formatters_).format(...)`. But `formatters_` is a member, and in a const method it's const. `std::get` on a const tuple returns a const reference. The element formatter's `format` must be const. For built-in types, it is. But for custom user types, the user's formatter's `format` might not be const. 

Hmm, this could be an issue. Let me check the actual fmt library - did they keep `format` const? Yes, a44c8f65 made it const. But this requires element formatters to have const `format`. 

Wait, but actually, looking more carefully - in the actual fmt library, this was eventually changed. Let me check the later versions. Actually, let me check if there's a problem with non-const-formattable element types.

Let me test with a custom type that has a non-const format:", "role": "assistant", "tool_calls": [{"function": {"arguments": "{"command":"cd /testbed && cat > /tmp/repro_custom.cpp << 'EOF'\n#include <tuple>\n#include <fmt/format.h>\n#include <fmt/ranges.h>\n\nstruct Custom {\n  int v;\n};\n\ntemplate <>\nstruct fmt::formatter<Custom> {\n  // non-const format\n  auto parse(format_parse_context& ctx) -> decltype(ctx.begin()) { return ctx.begin(); }\n  auto format(const Custom& c, format_context& ctx) -> decltype(ctx.out()) {\n    return fmt::format_to(ctx.out(), \"C{}\", c.v);\n  }\n};\n\nint main() {\n  std::tuple<Custom, Custom> t = std::make_tuple(Custom{1}, Custom{2});\n  std::string s = fmt::format(\"{}\", fmt::join(t, \", \"));\n  fmt::print(\"{}\\n\", s);\n}\nEOF\ng++ -std=c++17 -I/testbed/include /tmp/repro_custom.cpp /testbed/build/libfmt.a -o /tmp/repro_custom 2>&1 | head -20 && /tmp/repro_custom"}", "name": "bash"}, "id": "call_-7367038174536657895", "index": 0, "type": "function"}]}}], "created": 1700000138, "id": "synthesized-00138", "model": "glm-5.2", "object": "chat.completion", "request_id": "synthesized-00138", "usage": {"completion_tokens": 0, "prompt_tokens": 0, "total_tokens": 0}}
